newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Telecel sees low level of cancellations.
newsitem.headline: Telecel sees low level of cancellations.

text.p: Portuguese mobile phone operator Telecel-Comunicaccos Pessoais said it expected a rate of cancellations of between 20 and 25 percent in 1997, below the European average.

"In 1996, we had a rate of 18 percent which should rise towards the end of this year to between 20 and 25 percent, but even so it will be below the European average," chairman Antonio Carrapatoso told a news conference.
He said he expected the company to end the year with 550,000 clients, up from 455,585 at the end of June.
He said unpaid client bills were around 3.5 to four percent of turnover.
Telecel, which expects turnover of 80 billion escudos in 1997, said net profit in the first half of this year rose 127 percent to 5.85 billion escudos. Sales totalled 39.4 billion.

Carrapatoso forecast that the cellular phone business would increase market penetration by five percentage points during 1997. Total penetration, including Portugal Telecom's TMN was up 3.4 percent in the first six months at nine percent.

He said that the drop in sales per client, which fell 18 percent in the period to 15,119 escudos compared with the same 1996 period, was due to the entry of a new and different type of consumer, namely families, changes in tariffs and an increase in traffic.
